title: Generative AI in Higher Education: The ChatGPT Effect
extended_summary:
This book addresses the rapid emergence of ChatGPT and other generative AI tools and asks how they should be understood, governed, and used in higher education. Rather than testing a single classroom intervention, it synthesizes concepts, practical examples, policy issues, and technical background to help educators and institutions respond to GenAI’s impact on teaching, learning, assessment, and administration.

The approach is a broad conceptual and practice-oriented treatment of GenAI in higher education. It discusses AI literacy, the strengths and weaknesses of ChatGPT in curriculum design, redesigning assessment for the AI era, and developing institutional AI policies. The book also includes illustrative scenarios, prompts, and a framework for assessment integration, alongside a qualitative study of perceptions of GenAI policy in Hong Kong and a technical overview of how GenAI works.

The intended users are primarily higher-education educators, students, and administrators/policymakers, with examples centered on post-secondary contexts. The book’s main conclusion is that GenAI should be embraced thoughtfully as a partner to human teaching and assessment, supported by AI literacy, ethical policy, and redesigned pedagogy rather than used as a replacement for human judgment.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a book introduction/preview and review-style text about generative AI in higher education, not an empirical study. It contains no direct methodology, no sample, and no evaluated intervention or measured educational outcomes.
impact_tier_rationale: There is no direct empirical evidence of impact on middle school mathematics achievement or any other student outcome. The text is conceptual and policy-oriented rather than outcome-evaluative.
